flashcards.a: A minimal set of attributes that uniquely identifies each tuple of a relation.
Unique for every tuple; minimal (no proper subset is unique); values not null.
Data: raw facts and figures. Database: organised collection of related data stored for easy access and management.

flashcards.q: 1c Redundancy can be beneficial and harmful (2)
flashcards.a: Harmful: wastes storage, causes inconsistency and anomalies. Beneficial when controlled: faster reads, backup/fault tolerance.
Named, stored blocks of SQL/code kept in the database and run on demand. Written and managed by the DBA/developer to reuse logic, enforce rules and improve performance.

Three levels: external (user views), conceptual (whole logical schema), internal (physical storage). Data independence: change one level without affecting the one above (logical and physical independence).
SELECT: columns to return. FROM: table(s) used. WHERE: filter rows by condition.
Organising tables (1NF, 2NF, 3NF) to remove redundancy and anomalies, keeping data consistent.

Entities: Customer, Product, Order, Supplier, Employee. Customer 1—M Order; Order M—N Product (via Order_Item); Supplier 1—M Product; Employee 1—M Order (processes). Add keys such as CustomerID, OrderID.

flashcards.q: Q2 Database life cycle for Mama Ngina store system (20)
flashcards.a: 1 Requirements analysis; 2 conceptual design (ERD); 3 logical design (tables, keys, normalise); 4 physical design/implementation (DBMS, indexes); 5 data loading and testing; 6 deployment and training; 7 maintenance and backup. Tie each stage to the manager's daily-data needs.

flashcards.q: Q3a Relationship between CUSTOMER and ORDERS (2)
flashcards.a: One-to-many (referential link by CustomerID).

flashcards.q: Q3b Primary keys and foreign key (3)
flashcards.a: PK: CUSTOMER(CustomerID), ORDERS(OrderID). FK in ORDERS: CustomerID.

flashcards.q: Q3c Customer names with their orders (4)
flashcards.a: SELECT c.customer_name, o.order_id FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id;

flashcards.q: Q3d Total orders by John Mwangi (3)
flashcards.a: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o JOIN customer c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE c.customer_name='John Mwangi';  Result: 2

flashcards.q: Q3e Customer with highest total spend (4)
flashcards.a: SELECT c.customer_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS t FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_name ORDER BY t DESC LIMIT 1;  Result: John Mwangi (27,000)

flashcards.q: Q3f Why link by CustomerID, not names (4)
flashcards.a: IDs are unique, names can repeat or change; avoids ambiguity and update anomalies; saves space; enforces integrity.

flashcards.q: Q4a(i) Redundancy and anomalies in SALES_RECORD (2)
flashcards.a: Customer name/phone repeated for S01. Update anomaly (change phone in many rows), insertion anomaly (can't add product without a sale), deletion anomaly (deleting a sale loses customer data).
CUSTOMER(CustID, Name, Phone); PRODUCT(ProdID, Name, Price); SALE(SaleID, CustID FK); SALE_ITEM(SaleID, ProdID, Quantity). Total is derived (Quantity×Price).
DBMS storing data in related tables linked by keys, queried with SQL. Examples: MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQL Server.
OODBMS stores data as objects (with methods, inheritance) and suits complex data; RDBMS stores rows in tables and uses SQL.
CREATE TABLE student(id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(50)); ALTER TABLE student ADD age INT;  (also DROP, TRUNCATE)
% = zero or more characters; _ = exactly one character. WHERE name LIKE 'J%' ; WHERE name LIKE '_a%'

flashcards.q: Q5a(i) Names of students pursuing IT (2)
flashcards.a: SELECT Name FROM Student WHERE Code='CIT';  (Nathan)
SELECT Code, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Student GROUP BY Code ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1;  Result: CCS

flashcards.q: Q5b(i) Employees working for First Bank Corporation
flashcards.a: SELECT empname FROM Works WHERE companyname='First Bank Corporation';

flashcards.q: Q5b(ii) Name, street, city of those earning over 200000
flashcards.a: SELECT e.empname, e.street, e.city FROM Employee e JOIN Works w ON e.empname=w.empname WHERE w.companyname='First Bank Corporation' AND w.salary>200000;

flashcards.q: Q5b(iii) Employees living in the same city as their company
flashcards.a: SELECT e.empname FROM Employee e JOIN Works w ON e.empname=w.empname JOIN Company c ON w.companyname=c.companyname WHERE e.city=c.city;
Single: one value per entity (date of birth). Multi-valued: several values (phone numbers).
Derived: computed from another attribute (age from DOB). Non-derived: stored directly.

flashcards.q: Q5c(iii) Candidate key vs super key
flashcards.a: Super key: any attribute set that uniquely identifies tuples. Candidate key: a minimal super key.
Treating a relationship (with its entities) as a higher-level entity so it can take part in another relationship.
Top-down: splitting an entity into sub-entities with extra attributes (Employee into Manager, Clerk); uses ISA.
